prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Pasadena, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1465; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep my name off this, if that's okay. You can use the claim number.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving through the intersection in Pasadena, Texas, heading east on the main road. The light had been green for me when I entered.
Q: What happened next?
A: A car came from the cross street on my right side. It didn't stop, and it hit the passenger side of my vehicle. I didn't have time to react. My car spun a little and ended up against the curb.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle's signal before it entered the intersection?
A: No, I was watching the road ahead. I only saw it when it was already coming across.
Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle on your own?
A: Yes, but my right shoulder was hurting right away. I couldn't lift my arm without a sharp pain.
Q: Have you received medical treatment since the accident?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same day. They took X-rays and said it was probably a strain, but I've been referred to an orthopedic doctor for an MRI.
Q: Did you have any pain or shoulder problems before this collision?
A: No, not that I can recall. I play some recreational softball, but I hadn't had any trouble with that shoulder.
Q: Is there anything you would like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still having trouble sleeping on that side and doing simple things like reaching into a cabinet. I'd like to get this resolved.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
A: Okay, thank you.
